title: GPT-4 extracts reasons for missing anticoagulation from atrial fibrillation clinical notes
summary: Of 35,737 patients with atrial fibrillation in one health system, 7712 (21.6%) had no active oral anticoagulation prescription. Annotators labelled notes for 771 patients; GPT-4 with engineered prompts outperformed a trained ClinicalBERT (macro-F1 0.79 vs 0.69). Applied to the remaining notes, GPT-4 found a documented reason in 61.1%, most often alternative antiplatelet use (23.3%), therapeutic inertia (21.0%) and low AF burden (17.1%). The data come from a single health system and the inference-set output was not separately validated.
ai_technology: GPT-4 prompting and trained ClinicalBERT extracting reasons for anticoagulation nonprescription from clinical notes

evidence.tested: Models scored against three annotators' labels on a 10% annotation set, then run on the 90% inference set.
evidence.unknown: Single health system; accuracy on the inference set was not independently checked; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A large language model read clinical notes to classify why patients were not prescribed anticoagulants.
